about: THE RUNES - the Younger Futhark (long-branch and short-twig rows, the dotted runes, the older forms of the first finds), each with the sounds it stood for; and real inscriptions of the time with how they read.

inscriptions.runes: ᚢᛚᚠᚢᛦᛡᚢᚴᚢᚦᛁᚾᛡᚢᚴᚺᚢᛏᛁᚢᛦ ᚺᛁᛡᛚᛒᛒᚢᚱᛁᚾᛋᚢᛁᚦᛦ ᚦᛡᛁᛗᛏᚢᛁᛡᚱᚴᛁᛡᚢᚴᛏᚢᛁᚱᚴᚢᚾᛁᚢ ᛒᚢᚢᚱ
inscriptions.transliteration: ulfuʀAukuþinAukHutiuʀ HiAlbburinsuiþʀ þAiMtuiArkiAuktuirkuniu buur
inscriptions.normalized: Ulfr ok Óðinn ok Hó-Týr ... (the rest is read in different ways)
inscriptions.gloss: Names Ulfr, Odin and ‘High-Týr’, then asks for help against something harmful (a dwarf, or pain). Probably a charm. The second half is read differently by different scholars (Stoklund 1996, Grønvik 1999, Nordström 2021).
inscriptions.note: Gods' names in runes; because the reading is disputed, more than one answer can count.

inscriptions.runes: ᚦᚢᚱᛚᚠᚱ ᛬ ᚱᛁᛋᚦᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛏᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚦᚬᚾᛋᛁ ᛬ ᚼᛁᛘᚦᛁᚵᛁ ᛬ ᛋᚢᛁᚾᛋ ᛬ ᛂᚠᛏᛁᛦ ᛬ ᛂᚱᛁᚴ ᛬ ᚠᛁᛚᛅᚵᛅ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛁᛅᛋ ᛬ ᚢᛅᚱᚦ ᛬ ᛏᛅᚢᚦᚱ ᛬ ᚦᚬ ᛬ ᛏᚱᛂᚴᛁᛅᛦ ᛬ ᛋᛅᛏᚢ ᛬ ᚢᛘ ᛬ ᚼᛅᛁᚦᛅᛒᚢ ᛬ ᛁᛅᚾ ᛬ ᚼᛅᚾ ᛬ ᚢᛅᛋ ᛬ ᛋᛏᚢᚱᛁᛘᛅᛏᚱ ᛬ ᛏᚱᛂᚵᛦ ᛬ ᚼᛅᚱᚦᛅ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚦᚱ
inscriptions.transliteration: þurlfr : risþi : stin : þonsi : himþigi : suins : eftiʀ : erik : filaga : sin : ias : uarþ : tauþr : þo : trekiaʀ : satu : um : haiþabu : ian : han : uas : sturimatr : tregʀ : harþa : kuþr
inscriptions.normalized: Þórulfr reisti stein þenna, heimþegi Sveins, eptir Eirík, félaga sinn, er varð dauðr þá er drengir sátu um Heiðabý; en hann var stýrimaðr, drengr harða góðr.
inscriptions.gloss: Thorulf, King Svein's retainer, raised this stone for Erik, his partner, who died when warriors besieged Hedeby. Erik was a ship's master, a very good man.
inscriptions.note: Names a trading partner (félagi) and a ship's master (stýrimaðr); the siege of Hedeby dates it.

inscriptions.runes: ᚭᛋᚠᚱᛁᚦᚱ ᛬ ᚴᛆᚱᚦᛁ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛘᛒᛚ ᛬ ᚦᛆᚢᚿ ᛬ ᚭᚠᛏ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚴᛏᚱᛁᚴᚢ ᛬ ᛋᚢᚿ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚿ ᛬ ᚭᚢᛁ ᛬ ᚴᚿᚢᛒᚢ
inscriptions.transliteration: osfriþr : karþi : kumbl : þaun : oft : siktriku : sun : sin : oui : knubu
inscriptions.normalized: Ásfríðr gerði kuml þau ept Sigtrygg, son sinn, á vé Gnúpu. (or: ... son sinn ok Gnúpu)
inscriptions.gloss: Asfrid made this monument for Sigtrygg, her son, at Gnupa's holy place - or ‘her son and Gnupa's’: the word oui can be read either way.
inscriptions.note: Pairs with Hedeby 4 (two parts of one story). The double reading of oui is a ready-made puzzle.

inscriptions.runes: ᛋᚢᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚾᚢᚴᛦ ᛬ ᛋᛅᛏᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛏᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚢᚠᛏᛁᛦ ᛬ ᛋᚴᛅᚱᚦᛅ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚼᛁᛘᚦᛁᚵᛅ ᛬ ᛁᛅᛋ ᛬ ᚢᛅᛋ ᛬ ᚠᛅᚱᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚢᛂᛋᛏᚱ ᛬ ᛁᚬᚾ ᛬ ᚾᚢ ᛬ ᚢᛅᚱᚦ ᛬ ᛏᛅᚢᚦᚱ ᛬ ᛅᛏ ᛬ ᚼᛁᚦᛅ᛬ᛒᚢ
inscriptions.transliteration: suin : kunukʀ : sati : stin : uftiʀ : skarþa : sin : himþiga : ias : uas : farin : uestr : ion : nu : uarþ : tauþr : at : hiþa:bu
inscriptions.normalized: Sveinn konungr setti stein eptir Skarða, sinn heimþega, er var farinn vestr, en nú varð dauðr at Heiðabý.
inscriptions.gloss: King Svein set this stone for Skardi, his retainer, who had gone west, and then died at Hedeby.
inscriptions.note: ‘Gone west’ is a voyage to England; the king himself raised it.

inscriptions.runes: ᚬᛋᚠᚱᛁᚦᚱ ᛬ ᚴᛅᚱᚦᛁ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛒᛚ ᛬ ᚦᛅᚢᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛏᚢᛏᛁᛦ ᛬ ᚢᚦᛁᚾᚴᛅᚢᚱᛋ ᛬ ᚬᚠᛏ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚴᛏᚱᛁᚢᚴ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚾᚢᚴ ᛬ ᛋᚢᚾ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚴ ᛬ ᚴᚾᚢᛒᚢ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚱᛘᛦ ᛬ ᚱᛅᛁᛋᛏ ᛬ ᚱᚢᚾᛅᛦ
inscriptions.transliteration: osfriþr : karþi : kubl : þausi : tutiʀ : uþinkaurs : oft : siktriuk : kunuk : sun : sin : auk : knubu : kurmʀ : raist : runaʀ
inscriptions.normalized: Ásfríðr gerði kuml þessi, dóttir Óðinkárs, ept Sigtrygg konung, son sinn ok Gnúpu. Gormr reist rúnar.
inscriptions.gloss: Asfrid, Odinkar's daughter, made this monument for King Sigtrygg, her son and Gnupa's. Gorm carved the runes.
inscriptions.note: Second part of the Sigtrygg pair: gives the mother's father and the carver's name.

inscriptions.runes: ᚴᚢᚱᛘᛦ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚾᚢᚴᛦ ᛬ ᚴᛅᚱᚦᛁ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛒᛚ ᛬ ᚦᚢᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚦᚢᚱᚢᛁ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚾᚢ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾᛅ ᛬ ᛏᛅᚾᛘᛅᚱᚴᛅᛦ ᛬ ᛒᚢᛏ

inscriptions.normalized: Gormr konungr gerði kuml þessi ept Þyrvé, konu sína, Danmarkar bót.
inscriptions.translation: King Gorm constructed this barrow to his wife Thyre Danmarksbod.
inscriptions.note: ‘Danmarkar bót’ (Denmark's adornment or remedy): whose title is it, Thyra's or Gorm's?

inscriptions.runes: ᚼᛅᚱᛅᛚᛏᚱ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚾᚢᚴᛦ ᛬ ᛒᛅᚦ ᛬ ᚴᛅᚢᚱᚢᛅ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛒᛚ ᛬ ᚦᛅᚢᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚱᛘ ᚠᛅᚦᚢᚱ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚴ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚦᚬᚢᚱᚢᛁ ᛬ ᛘᚢᚦᚢᚱ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾᛅ ᛬ ᛋᛅ ᚼᛅᚱᛅᛚᛏᚱ ᛬ ᛁᛅᛋ ᛬ ᛋᚬᛦ ᛬ ᚢᛅᚾ ᛬ ᛏᛅᚾᛘᛅᚢᚱᚴ ᛬ ᛅᛚᛅ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚴ ᛬ ᚾᚢᚱᚢᛁᛅᚴ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚴ ᛬ ᛏᛅᚾᛁ ᚴᛅᚱᚦᛁ ᚴᚱᛁᛋᛏᚾᚬ
inscriptions.transliteration: haraltr : kunukʀ : baþ : kaurua : kubl : þausi : aft : kurm faþur sin : auk aft : þąurui : muþur : sina : sa haraltr (:) ias : soʀ : uan : tanmaurk : ala : auk : nuruiak : auk : t(a)ni (karþi) kristno
inscriptions.normalized: Haraldr konungr bað gera kuml þessi ept Gorm, fǫður sinn, ok ept Þyrvé, móður sína, sá Haraldr er sér vann Danmǫrk alla ok Norveg ok dani gerði kristna.
inscriptions.translation: King Harald caused this barrow to be made to his father Gorm, and his mother Thyre; the same Harald who acquired all Denmark, and Norway, and Christianity as well,
inscriptions.note: A king's claim to Denmark and Norway and the christening of the Danes; pairs with Gorm's stone beside it.

inscriptions.runes: ᛏᚢᚠᛅ ᛬ ᛚᛦᛏ ᛬ ᚴᛅᚢᚱᚢᛅ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛒᛚ ᛬ ᛘᛁᛋᛏᛁᚢᛁᛋ ᛬ ᛏᚢᛏᛁᛦ ᛬ ᚢᚠᛏ ᛬ ᛘᚢᚦᚢᚱ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾᛅ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚾᛅ ᛬ ᚼᛅᚱᛅᛏᛋ ᛬ ᚼᛁᚾᛋ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚦᛅ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚱᛘᛋ ᛬ ᛋᚢᚾᛅᛦ
inscriptions.transliteration: tufa : lʀt : kaurua : kubl : mistiuis : tutiʀ : uft : muþur : sina : kuna : harats : hins : kuþa : kurms : sunaʀ
inscriptions.normalized: Tófa lét gera kuml, Mistivís dóttir, ept móður sína, kona Haralds hins góða, Gorms sonar.
inscriptions.translation: Tuva caused this barrow to be constructed; she was a daughter of Mistivi; she made it to her mother, and was the wife of Harald the Good, son of Gorm.
inscriptions.note: A Wendish prince's daughter married to the Danish king: a link to Wendland (Reric, Starigard).

inscriptions.runes: ᚱᛅᚴᚾᚼᛁᛚᛏᚱ ᛬ ᛋᛅᛏᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛏᛅᛁᚾ ᚦᚬᚾᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚠᛏ ᛬ ᛅᛚᛅ ᛬ ᛋᛅᚢᛚᚢᛅ ᚴᚢᚦᛅ ᛬ ᚢᛁᛅ ᛚᛁᚦᛋ ᚼᛅᛁᚦᚢᛁᛅᚱᚦᛅᚾ ᚦᛁᛅᚴᚾ / ᛅᛚᛅ ᛬ ᛋᚢᚾᛁᛦ ᛬ ᚴᛅᚱᚦᚢ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛒᛚ ᛬ ᚦᛅᚢᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚠᛅᚦᚢᚱ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚴ ᛬ ᚼᚬᚾᛋ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚾᛅ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚢᛅᚱ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛋᚢᛏᛁ ᛬ ᚱᛅᛁᛋᛏ ᛬ ᚱᚢᚾᛅᛦ ᛬ ᚦᛅᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᛏᚱᚢᛏᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚦᚢᚱ ᛬ ᚢᛁᚴᛁ ᛬ ᚦᛅᛋᛁ ᛬ ᚱᚢᚾᛅᛦ / ᛅᛏ ᛬ ᚱᛁᛏᛅ ᛬ ᛋᛅ ᛬ ᚢᛅᚱᚦᛁ ᛬ ᛁᛋ ᛬ ᛋᛏᛅᛁᚾ ᚦᛅᚾᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛅᛁᛚᛏᛁ ᛬ ᛁᚦᛅ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚬᚾᚬᚾ ᛬ ᛏᚱᛅᚴᛁ
inscriptions.transliteration: raknhiltr : sati : stain þonsi : auft : ala : saulua kuþa : uia l(i)þs haiþuiarþan þiakn ¶ ala : suniʀ : karþu : kubl : þausi : aft : faþur : sin : auk : hons : kuna : auft : uar : sin : in : suti : raist : runaʀ : þasi : aft : trutin : sin : þur : uiki : þasi : runaʀ ¶ at : rita : sa : uarþi : is : stain þansi : ailti : iþa aft : onon : traki
inscriptions.normalized: Ragnhildr setti stein þenna ept Alla Sǫlva, goða véa, liðs heiðverðan þegn. Alla synir gerðu kuml þessi ept fǫður sinn ok hans kona ept ver sinn. En Sóti reist rúnar þessar ept dróttin sinn. Þórr vígi þessar rúnar. At ræti(?) sá verði er stein þenna elti(?) eða ept annan dragi.
inscriptions.translation: 1. “Raynhilde placed this stone to Ale Solvegolde, a man well deserving of honour.” 2. “The sons of Ale erected this barrow to their father, and his wife to her husband, but Sote inscribed these Runes to his lord. May Thor bless these Runes.” 3. “Accursed be he who moves this stone, or takes it to another place.”
inscriptions.note: Thor is asked to hallow the runes, and a curse guards the stone: a heathen-faith puzzle.

inscriptions.runes: ᚴᚢᚾ᛫ᚢᛅᛚᛏᛋ ᛋᛏᛅᛁᚾ ᛋᚢᚾᛅᛦ ᚱᚢᚼᛅᛚᛏᛋ ᚦᚢᛚᛅᛦ ᚬ ᛋᛅᛚᚼᛅᚢᚴᚢᛘ
inscriptions.transliteration: kun'uAlts stAin sunaʀ ruHalts þulaʀ o salHauku(m)
inscriptions.normalized: Gunnvalds steinn, sonar Hróalds, þular á Salhaugum.
inscriptions.translation: KUNUÆLT'S STONE, SON of-RUHALT, THYLE (Speaker, Priest) ON the-SALHOWS.
inscriptions.note: A þulr - a reciter of lore - near Lejre: ties to the hall lore contests.

inscriptions.runes: ᚱᚼᚢᚢᛚᚠᛦ ᛬ ᛋᛅᛏᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛏᛅᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚾᚢᚱᛅ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚦᛁ ᛬ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚦᚢᛘᚢᛏ ᛬ ᛒᚱᚢᚦᚢᚱ ᛬ ᛋᚢᚾᚢ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛏᚱᚢᚴᚾᛅᚦᚢ … ᛅᚢᛅᛁᛦ ᛬ ᚠᛅᚦᛁ
inscriptions.transliteration: rhuulfʀ : sati : stain : nura : kuþi : aft : kuþumut : bruþur : sunu : sin : truknaþu ... auaiʀ : faþi
inscriptions.normalized: Hróulfr setti stein, Nóra goði, ept Guðmund, bróðurson sinn. Drukknuðu ... Ávarr fáði.
inscriptions.translation: RHUULF SET this-STONE, of-the-NUR-men (or, of the NUR district) the GUTHI (Temple-chief and Magistrate), AFTER KUTHUMUT (= GUDMUND), BROTHER-SON (nephew) SIN (his). DROWNED (were drowned, perisht at sea) (with-him all, = himself and all his men). ÆUAIR FAYED (raised this stone and carved these runes).
inscriptions.note: A nephew and his men drowned at sea: a lost ship.

inscriptions.runes: ᚦᛁᛅᚢᚦᚢᛁ ᛬ ᚱᛅᛁᛋᚦᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛏᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚦᛅᚾᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛅᚠᛏ ᛬ ᚢᚦᛁᚾᚴᛅᚢᚱ ᛬ ᚠᚢᚦᚬᚱᚴᚼᚾᛁᛅᛋᛏᛒᛚᛘᛦ ᛬ ᚾᛁᚢᛏ ᛬ ᚢᛅᛚ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛘᛋ ᛬ ᚦᛘᚴᛁᛁᛁᛋᛋᛋᛏᛏᛏᛁᛁᛁᛚᛚᛚ ᛬ ᛁᛅᚴ ᛬ ᛋᛅᛏᛏ ᛬ ᚱᚢᚾᛅᛦ ᛬ ᚱᛁᛏ
inscriptions.transliteration: þiauþui : raisþi : stin : þansi : aft : uþinkaur : fuþorkhniastblmʀ : niut : ual : kums : þmkiiissstttiiilll : iak : satt : runaʀ : rit
inscriptions.normalized: Þjóðvé reisti stein þenna ept Óðinkár. fuþorkhniastblmʀ. Njót vel kumls! þmk iii sss ttt iii lll. Ek satta rúnar rétt.
inscriptions.gloss: Thjodve raised this stone for Odinkar. Then the whole row of 16 runes. ‘Make good use of the monument!’ Then a coded line (þmk iii sss ttt iii lll) that hides the charm-words þistill, mistill, kistill (thistle, mistletoe, casket). ‘I set the runes right.’
inscriptions.note: A full rune row on a stone - a place to learn the 16 runes - and a real runic cipher to break.

inscriptions.runes: ᛋᛅᚴᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛅᛏᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛏᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚦᛅᛋᛁ ᛬ ᚼᚢᚠᛏᛁᛦ ᛬ ᚬᛋᛒᛁᚢᚱᚾ ᛬ ᛋᛁᚾ ᛬ ᚠᛁᛚᛅᚵᚬ ᛬ ᛏᚢᚴᛅ ᛬ ᛋᚢᚾ ᛬ ᛋᛅᛦ ᛬ ᚠᛚᚢ ᛬ ᛅᚴᛁ ᛬ ᛅᛏ ᛬ ᚢᛒ᛬ᛋᛅᛚᚢᛘ ᛬ ᛅᚾ ᛬ ᚢᛅ ᛬ ᛘᛅᚦ ᛬ ᛅᚾ ᛬ ᚢᛅᛒᚾ ᛬ ᛅᚠᚦᛁ
inscriptions.transliteration: saksi : sati : stin : þasi : huftiʀ : osbiurn : sin : filago : tuka : sun : saʀ : flu : aki : at : ub:salum : an : ua : maþ : an : uabn : afþi
inscriptions.normalized: Saxi setti stein þenna eptir Ásbjǫrn, sinn félaga, Tóka son. Sá flýði eigi at Uppsǫlum, en vá meðan hann vápn hafði.
inscriptions.translation: Saxi on his mate Asborn, son of Toki: He fled not in the battle at Upsala, but fought whilst he had weapons.
inscriptions.note: A partner (félagi) who stood at the battle of Uppsala (Fýrisvellir, c. 985).

inscriptions.runes: ᛋᚢᛁᚾ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚴ ᛬ ᚦᚢᚱᚵᚢᛏᚱ ᛬ ᚴᛁᛅᚢᚱᚦᚢ ᛬ ᚴᚢᛒᛚ ᛬ ᚦᛁᛋᛁ ᛬ ᛂᚠᛏᛁᛦ ᛬ ᛘᛅᚾᛅ ᛬ ᛅᚢᚴ ᛬ ᛋᚢᛁᚾᛅ ᛬ ᚴᚢᚦ ᛬ ᚼᛁᛅᛚᛒᛁ ᛬ ᛋᛁᛅᚢᛚ ᛬ ᚦᛂᛦᛅ ᛬ ᚢᛂᛚ ᛬ ᛁᛅᚾ ᛬ ᚦᛂᛦ ᛬ ᛚᛁᚴᛁᛅ ᛬ ᛁ ᛬ ᛚᚢᚾᛏᚢᚾᚢᛘ
inscriptions.transliteration: suin : auk : þurgutr : kiaurþu : kubl : þisi : eftiʀ : mana : auk : suina : kuþ : hialbi : siaul : þeʀa : uel : ian : þeʀ : likia : i : luntunum
inscriptions.normalized: Sveinn ok Þorgautr gerðu kuml þessi eptir Manna ok Sveina. Guð hjalpi sál þeira vel. En þeir liggja í Lundúnum.
inscriptions.gloss: Svein and Thorgaut made this monument for Manni and Sveini. God help their souls well. And they lie in London.
inscriptions.note: Two men buried in London: whose graves? A link to the London stone (Cnut's Danes).

inscriptions.site: Rök stone (opening and the Theodric verse)
inscriptions.runes: ᛆᚠᛐ ᚢᛆᛙᚢᚦ ᛌᛐᚭᚿᛐᛆ ᚱᚢᚿᛆᛧ ᚦᛆᛧ ᚿ ᚢᛆᚱᛁᚿ ᚠᛆᚦᛁ ᚠᛆᚦᛁᛧ ᛆᚠᛐ ᚠᛆᛁᚴᛁᚭᚿ ᛌᚢᚿᚢ … ᚱᛆᛁᚦ ᚦᛁᛆᚢᚱᛁᚴᛧ ᚽᛁᚿ ᚦᚢᚱᛙᚢᚦᛁ ᛌᛐᛁᛚᛁᛧ ᚠᛚᚢᛐᚿᛆ ᛌᛐᚱᚭᚿᛐᚢ ᚽᚱᛆᛁᚦᛙᛆᚱᛆᛧ ᛌᛁᛐᛁᛧ ᚿᚢ ᚴᛆᚱᚢᛧ ᚭ ᚴᚢᛐᛆ ᛌᛁᚿᚢᛙ ᛌᚴᛁᛆᛚᛐᛁ ᚢᛓ ᚠᛆᛐᛚᛆᚦᛧ ᛌᚴᛆᛐᛁ ᛙᛆᚱᛁᚴᛆ
inscriptions.transliteration: aft uamuþ stonta runaʀ þaʀ n uarin faþi faþiʀ aft faikion sunu ... raiþ þiaurikʀ hin þurmuþi stiliʀ flutna strontu hraiþmaraʀ sitiʀ nu karuʀ o kuta sinum skialti ub fatlaþʀ skati marika
inscriptions.normalized: Aft Vámóð standa rúnar þær. En Varinn fáði, faðir, aft feigjan sun. ... Reið Þjóðríkr hinn þormóði, stillir flotna, strǫndu Hreiðmarar. Sitr nú gǫrr á gota sínum, skildi of fatlaðr, skati Mæringa.
inscriptions.translation: ‘After Wamuð stand Runes these, but Warin made [them] A-father for a-fey [dead] son.’ ... ‘Ruled Theodrick daring of mood, Lord of seamen, Redmere's strand! He sitteth now in full [war] gear on his steed, Shield girt, [the] Marings' Prince.’
inscriptions.note: The stone is itself a chain of riddles (‘I tell the tale ...’) with cipher runes: the hardest reading puzzle in the set.

inscriptions.normalized: Styggr gerði kuml þau ept Eyvind, son sinn. Sá fell austr með Eivísli. Víkingr fáði ok Grímulfr.
inscriptions.gloss: Stygg made this monument for Eyvind, his son. He fell in the east with Eyvisl. Viking and Grimulf coloured (made) it.
inscriptions.note: An early eastern voyage; one of the makers is named Víkingr.

inscriptions.normalized: Þorgerðr reisti stein þenna eptir Ásur, sinn móðurbróður, er endaðisk austr í Grikkjum. Góðr karl Gulli gat fimm sonu. Fell á Fœri frœkn drengr Ásmundr, endaðisk Ásurr austr í Grikkjum, varð á Holmi Halfdan drepinn, Kári varð at Uddi(?) ok dauðr Búi. Þorkell reist rúnar.
inscriptions.gloss: Thorgerd raised this stone for Assur, her mother's brother, who died in the east in Greece. Good Gulli had five sons: brave Asmund fell at Føri; Assur died east in Greece; Halfdan was killed on Holm (Bornholm (?)); Kari died at Oddi (?); and Bui is dead. Thorkel carved the runes.
inscriptions.note: Five brothers, five places of death: a ready-made multi-part puzzle (find each place).

inscriptions.translation: Sigrid let raise this stone for Sweyn her husband: ‘He often sailed to Singallia On a dear bark by Dumisness.’
inscriptions.note: A trader's route in one line: a costly cargo ship (knǫrr), round Domesnes, to Semgallia. Sail it to solve it.

inscriptions.normalized: Spjóti, Halfdan, þeir reistu stein þenna eptir Skarða, bróður sinn. Fór austr heðan með Ingvari; á Serklandi liggr sonr Eyvindar.
inscriptions.translation: Spjute and Halfdan raised this stone after Skarde their brother. He went eastward with Roar. In Serkland lies the son.
inscriptions.gloss: Our note: modern reading - he went east from here with Ingvar; Eyvind's son lies in Serkland.
inscriptions.credit: duchaillu1889 vol. 1, chapter notes (‘a bautastone with runes, in one end of a ship-form at Lilla Lundley in Lids, Södermanland’). Sö 131
inscriptions.note: Ingvar's doomed voyage east (c. 1036-1041): about 25 stones name it; a chain across many stones.

inscriptions.gloss: Ingifast had the stone cut for Sigvid, his father. He fell in Holmgard (Novgorod), the leader of a warship with his crew.
inscriptions.note: A ship's leader who died at Holmgard: an eastern trade-town clue.

inscriptions.normalized: Þorsteinn lét reisa stein þenna eptir sik sjalfan ok son sinn Hefni. Var til Englands ungr drengr farinn, varð þá heima at harmi dauðr. Guð hjalpi sálu þeira. Brúni ok Slóði þeir ristu stein þenna.
inscriptions.translation: ‘Thurstan let raise this stone after himself and his son Hefni, He did to England, a young lad, go, did then at home for woe die. God help their souls [mine and Hefni's], Bruni and Slothi they carved this stone.’
inscriptions.note: A young man went to England and came home to die: what did he bring back?

inscriptions.normalized: Styrkárr ok Hjǫrvarðr létu reisa þenna stein at fǫður sinn Geira, sem vestr sat í þingaliði. Guð hjalpi sálu.
inscriptions.translation: Sterkar and Hiorvardr erected this stone to their father, Geiri, who dwelt west, in Thikalid (Thingmannalid). God help his soul.
inscriptions.credit: duchaillu1889 vol. 1, caption of Fig. 310 (‘Kålstad, Upland’). U 668
inscriptions.note: Served in the þingalið, the paid Norse host of the English kings (1013-1066).

inscriptions.runes: ᛁᚾ ᚢᛚᚠᚱ ᚼᛅᚠᛁᛦ ᚬ ᚬᚾᚴᛚᛅᛏᛁ ᚦᚱᚢ ᚴᛁᛅᛚᛏ ᛏᛅᚴᛅᛏ ᚦᛁᛏ ᚢᛅᛋ ᚠᚢᚱᛋᛏᛅ ᚦᛁᛋ ᛏᚢᛋᛏᛁ ᚴᛅ◌ᛏ ᚦᛅ ◌◌◌◌ ᚦᚢᚱᚴᛏᛁᛚ ᚦᛅ ᚴᛅᛚᛏ ᚴᚾᚢᛏᚱ

inscriptions.normalized: En Ulfr hefir á Englandi þrjú gjald tekit. Þat var fyrsta þat er Tosti galt. Þá galt Þorketill. Þá galt Knútr.
inscriptions.gloss: And Ulf has taken three gelds (pay-offs) in England. The first was the one Tosti paid. Then Thorketil paid. Then Knut paid.
inscriptions.note: Three Danegelds in order, three leaders: a chain riddle with the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

inscriptions.gloss: Alli had this stone raised for himself. He took Knut's payment in England. God help his soul.
inscriptions.note: A man rich with English silver: Cnut's geld of 1018 (?).

inscriptions.transliteration: rahnualtr : lit : rista : runar : efʀ : fastui : moþur : sina : onems : totʀ : to i : aiþi : kuþ hialbi : ant : hena ¶ runa : rista : lit : rahnualtr : huar a : griklanti : uas : lis : forunki
inscriptions.normalized: Ragnvaldr lét rista rúnar eptir Fastvé, móður sína, Ónæms dóttur, dó í Eiði. Guð hjalpi ǫnd hennar. ¶ Rúnar rista lét Ragnvaldr. Var á Grikklandi, var liðs forungi.
inscriptions.gloss: Ragnvald had the runes cut for Fastvi, his mother, Onæm's daughter, who died at Ed. God help her soul. - Ragnvald had the runes cut; he was in Greece, leader of the troop.
inscriptions.note: A captain of the Varangians in Constantinople, home again: his tales and his silver.

inscriptions.normalized: Frísa gildar létu reisa stein þenna eptir Þor[kel, gild]a sinn. Guð hjalpi ǫnd hans. Þorbjǫrn risti.
inscriptions.gloss: The Frisians' guild-brothers had this stone raised for Thorkel, their guild-brother. God help his soul. Thorbjorn carved.
inscriptions.note: A merchants' guild named after the Frisians - the game's own start region - at Sigtuna. A second stone there (U 391) names the same guild.

inscriptions.normalized: Steinn sá er settr eptir Sibba góða, son Foldars, en hans liði setti at ... Folginn liggr hinn er fylgðu, flestr vissi þat, mestar dáðir dólga Þrúðar draugr í þeimsi haugi; munat Reið-Viðurr ráða rógstarkr í Danmǫrku Endils jǫrmungrundar ørgrandari landi.
inscriptions.gloss: This stone is set for Sibbi the Good, Foldar's son, and his men set it at ... Then a verse: In this mound lies hidden the warrior whom the greatest deeds followed (most men knew it); no more upright sea-king, strong in strife, will rule land in Denmark. The verse is built of kennings: ‘tree of Thrud's battles’ = warrior; ‘chariot-Odin of Endil's wide ground’ = sea-king.
inscriptions.note: The only full court-metre (dróttkvætt) stanza on a runestone: decode the kennings.

inscriptions.normalized: Hróðvísl ok Hróðelfr, þau létu reisa steina eptir sonu sína þrjá. Þenna eptir Hróðfoss. Hann sviku Blakumenn í útferð. Guð hjalpi sál Hróðfoss. Guð svíki þá er hann sviku.
inscriptions.gloss: Rodvisl and Rodelf had stones raised for their three sons. This one for Rodfos. The Blakumen betrayed him on a journey abroad. God help Rodfos's soul. God betray those who betrayed him.
inscriptions.note: Three stones for three sons (G 134, G 135, G 136): a three-part set. Who were the Blakumen?

inscriptions.normalized: Bjartfáan stæddu stein þenna Hegbjǫrn, brœðr Hróðvísl, Eysteinn, ...muarr(?), er hafa steina stadda ept Hrafn suðr fyrir Rufsteini. Kómu vítt í Eifor. Vífill bauð ...
inscriptions.gloss: Brightly painted, this stone was set up by Hegbjorn and his brothers Rodvisl, Eystein and ...muar, who have raised stones for Hrafn south of Rufstein. They came far into Aifor. Vifil commanded (?) ...
inscriptions.note: Names a rapid on the river road to Byzantium: the same rapid a Greek emperor's book names.

inscriptions.gloss: Two snake-bands of runes cut by Swedes (Varangians) on the harbour lion. Too worn to read.
inscriptions.note: An unreadable text: a puzzle about whose hand cut it, not what it says.

inscriptions.note: ‘Gaut made this and all in Man’: a boast that points to his other crosses (find them).
